clue.text: Demented bloke in charge

blocks.note: a bloke is a man, in British slang
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A crazed fellow is running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' looks like a container signal, but it is the abbreviation i/c.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes wild, frenzied behaviour, so crazed or demented in everyday use.

clue.text: Heroin features in cocaine gag

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear within it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: H is slang for heroin
coke is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: A drug-dealing joke involving heroin and cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like a joke, but it is the verb to retch or choke.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to retch or have the throat close up, which is what choking does; a synonym.

clue.text: Associate to bury china with foreign article

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: Someone helps bury a set of crockery with an overseas newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is porcelain, not the country, and Ming is the prized dynasty's ware.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermingle is to mix and mingle with others, so to associate socially; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Like top man and his unnamed son giving cost before haggling

indicators.note: unnamed means without a name, so the letter standing for name is removed

blocks.note: as means like
the king is the top man of a realm
ties the son to the king
a king's son is a prince

explanation.surface: A monarch and his anonymous son put a price tag on something before bargaining.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name, so the unnamed prince loses his N.
explanation.definitionFit: The asking price is the figure a seller first names, which buyers then try to bargain down.

clue.text: Colt maybe raised wretchedly by side of mountain

indicators.note: something done wretchedly is botched, so these letters come out jumbled
the side of a word is one of its edge letters, here the first

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the opening letter of mountain

explanation.surface: A young horse brought up miserably on a mountainside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' looks like a young horse, but the capital points to Colt the gunmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A Colt revolver is carried in a holster at the hip, which is an example of a sidearm.

clue.text: Delay writer following our group in South Dakota

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so these pieces go within another
following means coming after, so one piece is written behind the other

blocks.note: us is our group
a pen is a writing tool
SD is the postal code for South Dakota

explanation.surface: An author holds up our party's tour of South Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the pen, not an author; 'our group' is simply us. SD is the postal abbreviation for the American state.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to put it off or halt it for a time, so to delay it.

clue.text: Slander constant smoker in a city

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: c is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
taken as written
a lum is a chimney in Scots, something that smokes
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A chain smoker in some city is badmouthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' is not a person but a chimney: LUM is the Scottish word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is a false and damaging statement about someone, the same thing as slander.
